DEGRADATION DOCTRINE (docs/REINTERP_AUDIO_PRODUCTION_GUIDE_2026-07-11.md §4, binding): every real filename referenced below is the DEGRADED (`_tape97`-suffixed) master generated by tools/degrade_audio.sh from the pristine original in assets/audio/ — SYSTEM audio stays clean elsewhere in the piece, but audio heard as coming off one of THESE physical tapes is always degraded first. WITNESS SYMMETRY (binding, ERA_MINING FIND #4, R28-2 spec §3/§6): Tape A and Tape B file 'playedThrough' (reached the tail after their last segment) or 'stoppedMidway' (play started — elapsedSec > 0 — then stopped/ejected/era-shifted before the tail) to ledger.tapes; a tape that is never pressed to PLAY (inserting it alone does not count) files NOTHING. It claimed Tape A was 'approximate by design' and that Tapes B and C were 'precisely synced to the real audio'. Measured against word-level Whisper transcripts of the actual recordings (tools/sync-lyrics.mjs), Tape A's captions sat on a perfect 10-second grid and ran 27 SECONDS LATE by the final line — the last caption was due to appear after the song had already ended, which is what Sérgio heard as 'very slow to start playing, can only hear the noise'. Tape B drifted up to +2.6s and Tape C up to +1.3s, so 'precisely synced' was not true of them either. Every `at` on a segment carrying audio is now MEASURED from the recording. ⚑ THE RULE THE TOOL OBEYS: timings come from Whisper, TEXT NEVER DOES. Whisper hears 'Hold my hands' where the authored lyric is 'Fold my hands'; that is a transcription artifact and the authored words stand. ⚑ RESOLVED 2026-08-21 — THESE CAPTIONS ARE CANON, THE TRANSCRIPT IS NOT. Whisper transcribes Tape C's opening as 'Restore the HOPE… restore the JOY you understand'; Sérgio confirmed the authored lyric is 'Restore the HOME and restore the plan / Restore the CHILD you understand / Restore the life that you demand / We'll make the silence sound like love.' Both are mishearings of a sung recording. DO NOT 'correct' these lines toward any transcript — a machine transcription of a song is evidence about TIMING and about nothing else. Six of Tape C's captions could not be matched at all and keep their authored times. Fine-grained resync is a polish pass, not blocking.

tapes._doc: SWAPPABLE CANDIDATE (Session 32) — Sérgio is producing alternate versions of this broadcast jingle; the CURRENT candidate is 'Discover The New You' (Pc_Simulation/Sources/Jingle_Brand New/Discover_The_New_You.mp3), degraded via `tools/degrade_audio.sh --tape97` — registered as discover_the_new_you_tape97_radio.mp3 in src/audio/tapeAudio.ts. Swapping in a new version requires: (1) run the degrade tool on the new source, (2) add one REGISTRY line in tapeAudio.ts, (3) point every segment's `audio` field below at the new filename — nothing else changes. Captions below are the ACTUAL SONG LYRICS (from discover_the_new_you.txt's word-level LRC), timed against its real ~28.63s duration — this SUPERSEDES the previous session's ad-copy-style captions (period-shifted from data/dialog/s2_media.json's Pastor Dale/Announcer/testimony lines), since honest captions must match what's actually audible on the real recording; the earlier ad-copy framing is preserved in `01_SESSION_LOG.md` history but not reproduced here. Filed both ways — also satisfies the guide's `tape` message like Tape A. ⚑ S89: the `--wrap` dial-tuning burst that used to bookend this file is REMOVED — Sérgio, 2026-08-15: the jingle has a scratching sound at the start, 'we already decided on that', remove it (a decision already taken, not reopened here). The file is now the plain --tape97 degrade with no head/tail static, so every caption `at` below drops the wrap's old 1.3s head offset and uses the song's own raw LRC timing. The old wrap-static bracket captions (`b-tuning-in`/`b-tuning-out`) also carried a SECOND, separate bug: `b-tuning-out`'s `audio:null` sat BEFORE the real clip's natural end, so `syncTapeAudio()` (src/engine/app.ts) tore the clip down (`setClip(null)`) the instant that segment went active — the tail of 'the new you' was being cut off mid-instrumental, which is Sérgio's separately-reported 'New you is cut off in its last seconds' fault. Both faults shared one cause (the wrap) and are fixed together: `b-tuning-out` is dropped, AND `realDurationSec` (below) floors the tape's own totalSeconds() at the real clip's actual end (2.2s start + 28.63s duration = 30.83s) — TAIL_SECONDS(3) alone would still have ended the tape at 26.05s (23.05 + 3), 2.6s before the clip finishes, so both fixes were needed, not just dropping the segment. `shelfLabel` (new field, PLACEHOLDER-draft) is the OTHER named fault this session — 'how does it label each of the tapes so we know which one to play?' — shown on hover/press before the tape is inserted (src/engine/app.ts).
